posts.trend: ₹500 coffee, ₹25,000 fitness, ₹40,000 rent: Is Gen Z really spending too much?
posts.context: Parents forward articles criticising gym expenses without realising that at 30, fitness is spinal maintenance for a 10-hour desk job.
posts.angle: What finance articles and parents call vanity fitness spending is actually basic mechanical upkeep for a sitting job.

landing_options.line: "Papa, yeh shauk nahi hai. Reedh ki haddi ki EMI hai."
30 ke baad gym shauk nahi, garam patti ka substitute hai.
Paidal chalne ke liye pehle footpath toh ho.
Aapka gym nahi, aapki sitting job ka repair bill hai.

slides: Subah 7 baje Papa ne article bheja: "Gym pe paisa barbaad."
Forward: "Aajkal ke bachche fitness pe ₹25,000 uda rahe hain. Hamare time mein subah daudte the."
"Papa, yeh shauk nahi hai. Reedh ki haddi ki EMI hai."
posts.caption: Send this to the friend whose parents think physiotherapy is a rich-people hobby.

messages.text: Dekho aajkal ke bachche ₹25,000 gym mein uda rahe hain. Subah park mein chala karo.
Papa office ke baad 9 baje park mein sirf kutte hote hain
Phir bhi, paise bachao. Yeh body shody mein kuch nahi rakha.
Papa body nahi bana raha, kamar sidhi rakhne ki kisht bhar raha hoon.

posts.rank_verdict: It relies on a first-person comeback to Dad rather than the account's second-person voice, and the 'not X, it is Y' frame is familiar.
